title: The purpose of frontier safety frameworks

opening.headline: Understand what the safety frameworks published by model providers mean for our organization's access to features and terms of use.
body: The model provider publishes a document titled Safety Framework. The document seems distant from our daily work, as it talks about the serious damage that even the most powerful models can cause. However, this document may affect which features are opened, when, and under what conditions.

In this class, the frameworks of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind will be placed on the same framework to compare their purpose and composition. Next, we will look at what the risk areas and capability thresholds are, what safety measures are in place when the thresholds are reached, and explain the impact of access-restricted functions on work plans through examples.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the purpose of the 3rd party Frontier Safety Framework
Distinguish how the framework affects access to features and conditions of use

screens.title: What does a provider’s safety framework mean to my organization?
screens.lead:
Read below and consider why this seemingly distant document is relevant to our work.

As of 2026-10, RSP v3.4 is a policy that reads together Risk Mitigation Measures, Frontier Safety Roadmap, and Risk Reports. Descriptions of past ASL stages do not determine all current training and deployment conditions.

visual.alt: A scene where a document in the distance casts a shadow over a work plan.

paragraphs: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind each release documents titled Safety Frameworks. The document talks about the fatal risks that even the most powerful models can pose. So, if you only read the document, it feels like a story that is far from our meeting minutes summary or report writing.

However, the promises made in this document may affect which features providers open, when and under what conditions. Requests in some areas may be monitored more strictly, certain features may be opened only to verified users, or releases may be delayed.
The goal of this lesson is to help you understand the purpose of the framework and explain how it connects to our work plan.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: If a document reaches us without us having to read it, what does it look like?

screens.outro: First, let's organize our thoughts on the standards of control.

screens.title: If the model continues to get stronger, by what criteria will it be controlled?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: How can we tell how much our abilities have improved?
items.answer: Measurements are needed. All three company frameworks have procedures for assessing capabilities in specific areas. I'm not saying it's dangerous based on intuition, but the starting point is to set a measurable standard in advance.

items.prompt: What do you need to be more careful about as your abilities increase?
items.answer: The higher the power, the greater the damage when misused. Therefore, we specifically select and track areas that could lead to serious damage. Examples include fields such as biology and chemistry, cybersecurity, and AI self-improvement.

items.prompt: Who should have access and under what conditions?
items.answer: For models with higher capabilities, access conditions are divided rather than being opened to everyone under the same conditions. Monitor usage, open only to trusted users, or limit permissions. This is a safety device that appears as a condition for accessing and using the function.

screens.outro: Now let’s put the frameworks of all three companies on the same table.

screens.title: Putting three frameworks on the same table
screens.lead: The table below organizes the frameworks of the three companies into the same category. Read along the horizontal lines and notice that although the names and terms are different, the structure is similar.

data.notes: The OpenAI Model Specification and Claude's Charter, which cover behavioral principles, are documents that determine how the model will behave. It has a different purpose than the Framework, which is a commitment to control based on competency levels.

screens.outro: Now that we have identified the common framework, let's take a closer look at risk areas and capability thresholds.

screens.title: Risk areas and capability thresholds
screens.lead: Move the slider to cycle through the four steps the framework addresses risk.

visual.alt: An illustration showing how the ability increases and safety devices are added when the threshold line is exceeded.
labels: When this capability is reached, current safety measures are insufficient.

stops.body: A risk area is an area of ability that can lead to serious harm. OpenAI tracks biology and chemistry, cybersecurity, and AI self-improvement. It explains that the criteria for prioritization are that risks must be plausible, measurable, serious, novel, immediate, or irreversible. Its characteristic is that it focuses on the most serious risks rather than all risks.

Create a threat model in each area and establish measurable criteria that will indicate when the model becomes capable enough to pose a real risk. Google DeepMind has procedures in place to detect when competency levels are reached throughout the model lifecycle. Evaluation continues before and after the model is released.

The threshold is a signal that when this capability is reached, current safety measures are insufficient. OpenAI sets two thresholds: high capability and lethal capability. Anthropic must base its judgment on the current RSP's risk categories and actions and public reports. Google DeepMind calls these core competency levels.

Once the threshold is reached, steps follow to ensure that safeguards are sufficient. OpenAI says it will not deploy models that have reached a high capability threshold until the risk is sufficiently reduced. Once Google DeepMind reaches core competency level, it conducts a safety review to ensure risks are reduced to a manageable level prior to external release. Distribution will be restricted until safeguards are in place.

screens.outro: Let's take a look at what safety devices actually apply after the threshold.

screens.title: Safeguards and Deployment Conditions: The Path to Functional Access and Usage Conditions
screens.lead: Select each tab to see the type of safeguard and what it looks like to the user.

tabs.label: Usage Monitoring
tabs.body: This is the first type of safeguard introduced by the OpenAI framework. When we fail to prevent models from assisting with harmful tasks, we monitor and respond to harmful requests by elevating them to human review. Users may see requests in some areas being rejected or checked more rigorously.

tabs.label: Trust-based approach
tabs.body: This is a method of screening who accesses the model. This includes opening up capabilities only to users who have established a trustworthy customer relationship. Users may see certain features as only open to verified users and subject to an application and approval process.

tabs.label: System design and limited privileges
tabs.body: This is a method of limiting the tools and permissions used by the model at the design stage. It lowers risk by reducing the path through which something harmful can be done. To the user, the agent's permissions appear to be narrowly set.

tabs.label: Anthropic's multi-layer safety system
tabs.body: Anthropic explains that it requires security measures such as internal access control and protecting model weights when thresholds are reached. On the distribution side, it is announced that multi-layered safety measures such as real-time monitoring, post-monitoring, and pre-red team are planned. The RSP page notes that the policy has been revised several times and that risk reports are also published.

tabs.label: What the user sees
tabs.body: Taken together, the framework reaches us as changes in functions and conditions without having to read it directly. Requests in some areas are blocked, certain features are only opened to verified users, or the release date is delayed. Therefore, the framework can be viewed as a background rule that determines the access conditions and scope of use of the functions provided by the supplier.

screens.outro: Let's look at an example of how background rules translate into actual business planning.

screens.title: Commentary: Functions and work plans with restricted access
screens.lead: The instructor walks you through the process of creating a plan for access restrictions in an example of automating security checks. Select the right arrow to see the steps.

steps.title: Check the situation
steps.body: Our team is looking to introduce an AI agent to automate security checks. The plan is to entrust the task of finding vulnerabilities and organizing inspection results. Let's look at how this usage fits into the provider's framework.

steps.title: Check overlap with stage 1 risk areas
steps.body: This application is in the area of cybersecurity. This is an area that OpenAI places in its tracking category, and Anthropic and Google DeepMind also address similar areas of risk. In other words, the capabilities we are trying to use overlap with areas that the framework sees as risk areas.

steps.title: Phase 2 Impact Expected
steps.body: If there is an overlap, requests in those fields may be subject to stronger monitoring or may be subject to conditions that open access only to verified users. Some requests may be denied. Anticipate this possibility in advance during the planning stage.

steps.title: Reflected in the 3rd stage schedule
steps.body: Schedule access requests, how long it will take for approval, and alternative means. Prepare alternative solutions so that work does not stop if access is not granted or is delayed.

steps.title: 4 stages of separation
steps.body: Separate steps that depend on blocked functions so that the entire work does not stop even if some functions are blocked. The organizing and reporting steps, which can be performed even without blocked functions, are performed separately.

steps.title: Instructor's judgment
steps.body: The more areas requiring functionality overlap with risk areas, the more likely it is that access conditions will be attached. However, this does not mean that we give up on introducing it, but we ensure that we have room in our plans by including the application process and alternative means in our schedule. The terms of access are set by the provider, so what we have control over is the schedule and design of alternatives.

screens.outro: Next, we will outline how changes in usage conditions affect the plan.

screens.title: Commentary: How changing conditions of use will affect your plans
screens.lead: The instructor unpacks four ways your plan can be affected when conditions of use change. Select the right arrow to check them one by one.

steps.title: Addition of Path 1 safety devices
steps.body: When a capacity threshold is reached, safeguards are added, such that some requests are rejected or monitoring is increased. This means that the same request may have been accepted before but rejected later. Plans need room to absorb these changes. It is important not to build your schedule on the assumption that certain requests will always be made.

steps.title: Path 2 Trust-Based Approach
steps.body: Once functional access is trust-based, application and approval processes become part of the work schedule. Waiting periods for approval are out of our control, so we leave a buffer period in our schedule.

steps.title: Path 3 Supporting Documents
steps.body: The plan is based on the risk areas and threshold criteria published by the provider in the framework document. Make your judgment by reading the promises made public by the provider, not rumors or speculation. The three companies are compared using the questions of measurement, mitigation, judgment, and disclosure, but do not assume that the intensity of obligations and goals are the same.

steps.title: Path 4 Behavioral Principles Document
steps.body: Behavioral principles documents, such as the OpenAI Model Specification and Claude's Charter, influence how the model follows instructions. These documents address how the model will behave, not controls based on ability level. Compare the expected behavior against the principles in this document.

steps.title: organizing
steps.body: Frameworks reach us as changes in functions and conditions without having to read them directly. Work plans therefore need room and alternative means to absorb changes in access conditions. Keeping a list of which features you rely on from which provider will help you quickly find which steps are affected.

screens.outro: Now that we've covered all the routes, let's summarize the highlights.

screens.title: Key takeaway: A framework is a promise of control
screens.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class. Read on to remember the initial question and why this seemingly distant document affects our plans.

paragraphs: The Frontier Safety Framework is a commitment to control that is applied as the model becomes more capable. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind assess risk and describe responses, but their specific threshold conditions, obligations, and goals are different.

Post-threshold safeguards appear in functional access and usage conditions in the form of usage monitoring, trust-based access, and restricted permissions. So, even without reading the documentation directly, it reaches us with rejections of some requests, features opening only to verified users, and delays in release times. While the behavioral principles document addresses the behavior of the model, the framework addresses controls by capability level.

callout.label: standards to remember
callout.text: The work plan includes allowances for access application periods and alternative means to allow for changes in access conditions.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: What best describes the competency threshold in the framework?
options: Maximum length of input the model can process at one time
Once this capability is reached, it will be a signal that the current safety devices are insufficient.
Upper limit on the number of requests a user can make per day
Rules that determine the tone in which the model follows instructions
checks.explain: Once critical mass is reached, stronger security and deployment safeguards are required. Measuring capabilities and strengthening controls at critical mass are the common framework.

wrong.0: Input length is a different concept from the thresholds covered by the safety framework.
wrong.2: Usage limits are a concept of rate plans.
wrong.3: How a model behaves is covered by behavioral principles documents such as the Model Specification or Charter.

checks.intro: Put your planning steps in the right order. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: When introducing security check automation agents, make sure you plan for access restrictions in the right order.
items: Determine if your usage overlaps with the framework's risk areas
Expect strong monitoring or verified user access conditions
Scheduling access requests, approval timelines, and alternative means
Separate steps that depend on blocked functions
checks.explain: First, identify overlap with risk areas and estimate impacts, then incorporate approval processes and alternatives into the schedule, and separate steps so that if some functions are blocked, the whole thing doesn't come to a halt.

glossary.def: This is how OpenAI tracks and prepares for advanced capabilities that could cause significant harm.
Anthropic's risk governance policy. Read the applied version and specific actions/goals separately.
This is how Google DeepMind identifies and detects capability levels and prepares response plans.
These are fields of capabilities that can lead to serious damage, such as biology, chemistry, cyber, and autonomous research and development.
When this level is reached, it is a baseline where the current safety measures are considered insufficient.

misconceptions.myth: Frameworks are a distant topic that has nothing to do with general work.
misconceptions.fact: Frameworks reach us as changes in functions and conditions without having to read them directly. This includes rejection of some requests, features opening only to verified users, and delays in launch times.

misconceptions.myth: The Framework and Model Behavioral Principles documents are the same thing.
misconceptions.fact: One deals with control over ability levels, and the other deals with how the model will behave. The OpenAI Model Specification and Claude's Charter are behavioral principles documents.

misconceptions.myth: The three companies' frameworks are completely different approaches.
misconceptions.fact: Although the terminology is different, they share the framework of defining risk areas, measuring capabilities, and strengthening safeguards at thresholds.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: A framework is a promise of control that applies as capabilities increase.
All three companies use the same framework of measurements, thresholds, and safeguards.
After the threshold, safety devices are expressed as conditions for access and use of functions.
The work plan leaves room and alternative means to absorb changes in access conditions.
